highlights.title: Helping robots fit into the human workplace
highlights.summary: Founded by Anthony Jules ’92, SM ’92 and Professor Emeritus Rodney Brooks, Robust AI’s robots are designed to collaborate with humans in factories and warehouses.
body: Images for download on the MIT News office website are made available to non-commercial entities, press and the general public under a Creative Commons Attribution Non-Commercial No Derivatives license. Despite fears about robots replacing humans at work, there are still plenty of things humans can do far better than machines. That’s fine with Robust AI, a startup building robots designed to complement what humans do best.

The company’s mobile robot, named Carter, resembles a utility cart on wheels and is designed to fit seamlessly alongside humans in fast-changing warehouse and factory environments. Carter features a force-sensitive handlebar for easy guidance, an AI-powered vision system, and holonomic wheels for instant movement in any direction.
As a result, humans can cut Carter off, push and pull it in any direction with one hand, and direct it with gestures or the onboard touch screen.

highlights.title: Supercell CEO believes Digital Fairness Act will hurt consumers
highlights.summary: Supercell CEO Ilkka Paananen, who last year proclaimed new EU policies risked killing Europe’s games sector, has said newly revealed proposals on the Digital Fairness Act will hurt consumers.
body: The European Union has published a draft proposal for the DFA, calling for changes to in-game currencies to more clearly state their value, disclose loot box odds and give users ability to turn off loot boxes - with all IAPs disabled by default for minors.

Supercell has been a champion of the free-to–play mobile space since launching Hay Day and Clash of Clans back in 2012, making billions of dollars in the years since. It’s become one of the region’s most successful gaming companies.
Paananen said while the European Commission promises to protect consumers with new regulations, the opposite will happen.
He claimed that by making it harder for players to buy something, there will be fewer free games on the market. Around 95% of Supercell’s monthly players play for free.

The use of algorithms to design structures has led to new parts optimized for ultralight aircraft, high-bandwidth antennas, and F1 racing cars.

But the best algorithmic design techniques still require lots of computation and time: Users only see the final design after it’s complete, after which they often must start the design process all over again to make changes. That process also makes it harder to trust that the final designs are structurally sound.

MIT researchers are making algorithmic designs more collaborative with a system that acts like an AI copilot. As the algorithm is generating the structure, it presents regions to the human designer for feedback.

highlights.title: ‘Pretty weird’: How a viral video shows a striking discrepancy in men and women’s knitwear
highlights.summary: Men are routinely getting more wool for their money – are women really paying a pink tax when they buy a jumper? • Don’t get Fashion Statement delivered to your inbox? Sign up here. It’s officially cosy season.
body: It’s officially cosy season. But before you treat yourself to a new wooly jumper, you may want to take a closer look at the care label.
Abercrombie & Fitch is facing a pink tax backlash, sparked by a video on TikTok that highlights the difference between the materials used in menswear and womenswear jumpers that cost the same.

Last month, while browsing the American brand’s site, Rachael Brownfield, a fashion content creator, noticed that it was selling a 100% merino wool jumper in its menswear section for $95 (£71), while a jumper for the same price in the womenswear section consisted of only 30% wool. While the styles of jumpers are different, they were marketed alongside each other in a social media post.

“Pretty weird,” she wrote below a video in which she questioned why a synthetic women’s jumper should cost the same as a men’s jumper made of pure wool. The Guardian has approached Abercrombie & Fitch for comment.

Rob Hawkins had revealed during the tournament that England had a ladder in their team room, marking each victory by spray painting a rung gold.

highlights.title: Fable Is Looking A Lot Darker Than We Expected
highlights.summary: Amid a modest 25th-anniversary celebration, Xbox dropped a new preview of the Fable reboot. This snippet — which runs for under four minutes — offers plenty of gameplay and a closer look at some of the ghoulish enemies you'll face, set in a slice of Albion that looks surprisingly grim compared to…
body: "The Hero of Briar Hill has entered the depths of Deepwood alongside Arden, a local Hero, to investigate why strange magical happenings have been troubling the people of Oakshire," the video synopsis reads. "Here, they cross a threshold where the natural magic of Deepwood appears corrupted by an outside force, and they discover hints as to who or what could be responsible."

One thing to note about this snippet of gameplay is that it's pulled from the PC build of Fable, with the settings cranked up to Ultra. It's a pretty good-looking glimpse of what you can expect from Fable next year, even if it feels different from its cheekier predecessors and more like a feudal action slice reminiscent of Control Resonant toward the end, with its red-hued aesthetic.

Of course, four minutes of Fable doesn't tell the whole story, and with the main campaign alone estimated to take 20 hours to finish, that doom-and-gloom feeling probably won't be present throughout the entire game.

highlights.title: Silicon Valley Is Still Defending Jensen Huang
highlights.summary: Nvidia employees and tech insiders never thought the chip king would lose his job. Despite his sudden resignation, many of them are still in denial.
body: News of Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged asset of China’s Ministry of State Security was first met with a muted response in Silicon Valley —including inside Nvidia itself. Huang’s resignation, after news of two other alleged romantic relationships with Nvidia staffers, has left both the company and the broader AI industry stunned.

As revelations about Huang’s initial affair came out earlier this week, rank-and-file Nvidia employees at first pursued business as usual, according to two current and three former employees at the chipmaker, speaking anonymously to protect relationships at the company. They trusted the board to investigate and act accordingly, but few workers thought Huang would actually leave.

Nvidia’s roughly 60,000 employees are loyal to the point that its global turnover rate is reportedly among the lowest in tech. Workers say they have heard it called having “green in your blood” or being “green-pilled” or on “team green,” referring to the company’s signature color. Huang was the company’s soul and the founder who stuck with it through challenges for 33 years. Employees appreciated that he kept layoffs rare and red tape sparing.
points: Nvidia employees and tech insiders never thought the chip king would lose his job.
Despite his sudden resignation, many of them are still in denial.

highlights.title: Kohli out for duck in triple-wicket-maiden as India hammered by NZ
highlights.summary: New Zealand's Matt Henry reduced India to 0-3 by inflicting ducks on Virat Kohli, Rohit Sharma and Shreyas Iyer during a stunning first-over triple-wicket-maiden as the tourists crumpled to 89 all out in a 244-run thrashing in the fourth ODI.
body: Chasing 334 in Mount Maunganui to take an unassailable 3-0 lead in the five-match series, India's reply got off to a dreadful start when seamer Henry's first delivery squared up Rohit and induced an edge to Finn Allen in the slip cordon.
Kohli survived the next three balls, although the first whistled past his outside edge, only to then be bowled by a nip-backer that kept low from the fifth delivery of Henry's over.

The Kiwi bowler, who earned his best ODI figures of 6-27, then trapped India captain Shreyas lbw with the final ball of the over, to set India on their way to their second-heaviest ODI defeat, after the 245-run drubbing by Sri Lanka in Sharjah in October 2000.

Henry was unable to complete a hat-trick with Ishan Kishan seeing off the first delivery of the 34-year-old's second over - another nip-backer which rattled Kishan on the thigh pad, too high for a genuine lbw appeal - but he went on to bowl the same batter for 27 in the 21st over when the left-hander inside-edged onto his leg stump.

highlights.title: Supercell and King bosses warn EU’s Digital Fairness Act could hurt players and studios
highlights.summary: King president Todd Green says Europe's 1,000-plus mobile studios face "dramatic consequences". UK trade body Ukie has also weighed in on the controversy.
body: Supercell boss Ilkka Paananen and King president Todd Green have hit back at the EU’s Digital Fairness Act, which the European Commission formally proposed on November 11.

The published proposal largely matches the leaked draft we reported on earlier this week. Paid-for virtual currencies would be switched off by default in games aimed at minors unless a parent approves, and loot boxes and pay-to-win mechanics would be banned for minors.

Games would also have to show the real-money value of virtual items, and let all players switch off loot boxes and addictive design features. In large-scale cases, the Commission would be able to fine companies up to 6% of their worldwide annual turnover.

The statements follow trade bodies Video Games Europe and the European Games Developer Federation calling the proposal “unworkable, unjustified and disproportionate”, and warning that it would be “game over for the European games industry”.

highlights.title: Before Anything Else, Geoffrey Holder Was a Painter. A New Show Spotlights His Tremendous Body of Work
highlights.summary: Guest curated by Dr. Erica Moiah James, the Museum of Contemporary Art North Miami’s “Geoffrey Holder: Black Magic” is the first museum survey to center the Tony-winning multihyphenate’s work as a visual artist.
body: Geoffrey Holder refused to choose a lane. Born in Trinidad and Tobago in 1930, he was a principal dancer with the Metropolitan Opera Ballet, the first Black man to win Tony Awards for both directing and costume design (for the Broadway hit The Wiz ), and the voice and face of 7Up throughout the 1970s and ’80s, all while building a celebrated film career with roles in Doctor Dolittle, Annie, and the Bond film Live and Let Die.

And yet, before everything else, Holder was a painter. “Painting always came first,” says his son, Leo Holder, who oversees the artist’s estate. “Practically everything else he did has always been an extension of this. He was always working on something. At any given time, wherever he was living, there were several canvases in progress.” Still, across his decades-long career, it was the facet of his work that received the least attention.

highlights.title: NFL quarterbacks are under more pressure than ever from rushers. Why?
highlights.summary: Despite all the advantages offenses have secured over the years, defenses are better at pressuring the QB than any other time in recent history. The Baltimore Ravens are preparing to start their fourth quarterback this year, Jacoby Brissett, against the beleaguered Los Angeles Chargers on Monday…
body: Jackson, Huntley and Fagnano were all injured after taking hits in games. And if it seems like quarterbacks are taking punishment more often this year, your eyes aren’t deceiving you. Through nine weeks, quarterbacks have been hit on 15.1% of their dropbacks, the most we’ve seen since 2006, when hits were first logged in official box scores.

That may be why more quarterbacks have started games through nine weeks in 2026 than in almost any other year in recent memory. This year’s 47 starters only fall behind 2019 (48 through nine weeks), 2010 (48) and 2007 (49) over the past 20 years, and the expected starts for Carson Beck, Kyle McCord and Fernando Mendoza will push the total up further.
It turns out that, despite all the advantages offenses have been given over the years, defenses are better at pressuring the quarterback than at any other time in recent NFL history.

highlights.title: ‘Women and War’ Follows Four Ukrainians’ Journeys Towards Healing From Trauma (Exclusive IDFA Trailer)
highlights.summary: "War does not end for these women when the weapons fall silent," highlights director Elwira Niewiera, whose doc about women going through long-term therapy premieres at IDFA in Amsterdam.
body: Four women in Ukraine who have survived Russia’s war. Four stories, including captivity, torture, sexual violence, times of hiding in dark basements, and the loss of loved ones. One shared journey – a journey toward healing. That is what the new documentary Women and War by Elwira Niewiera ( The Hamlet Syndrome, The Prince and the Dybbuk, The Domino Effect ) promises to take you on.

Women and War follows the journeys of Olena, Yuliia, Iryna, and Lena, who survived Russia’s ongoing war against Ukraine. Over the course of a year, the doc shows them going through long-term therapy in the remote mountains of the country as they slowly begin to heal under the care of therapists and psychologists. And each of them must follow her own path toward recovery as they confront the lasting impact of trauma in the hope of regaiingn emotional and physical balance. Can they overcome their struggles and reclaim their lives?

highlights.title: Farewell, Cybertruck: why the winding down of the ‘Maga hat on wheels’ is a sign of the times
highlights.summary: Eccentric and overhyped, Tesla’s Cybertruck became a stand-in for Elon Musk during his ascent in the Republican party. It will join the ranks of other vehicles symbolic of their eras – for better or for worse.
body: Three days after a historic blue tsunami changed America’s political landscape, Elon Musk announced Tesla would end production of its hulking Cybertruck next year.

Was it a coincidence? Maybe. Musk said the move was “to make room for increased Cybercab production”, referring to Tesla’s Robotaxi. But the combined circumstances felt highly appropriate: it was the end of an era.

Eccentric and overhyped, the Cybertruck became a kind of automotive stand-in for Musk himself amid his political ascent. Like so many of his projects, it was massively promoted, heavily delayed, and ultimately fell short: Musk once predicted he could sell 250,000 a year but ultimately sold 70,000 in three years, losing $1.9bn in the process, according to Quartz.

highlights.summary: Google says its new Gemini 4 Hydrogen model can give more helpful answers to complex questions, including "questions with multiple parts, hard-to-understand typos, or highly specific requests." The new model can break down your questions and address each part in its responses.
body: Google’s Robby Stein says Gemini 4 Hydrogen is ‘the biggest model upgrade to Search yet.’

Google says Gemini 4 Hydrogen also gives users a wider range of links in its responses by “conducting simultaneous queries across all the relevant subtopics.” Its responses have more visuals, too, like images, comparison tables, graphs, and maps. One of Stein’s examples shows the AI generating an interactive animated driving simulation in response to a user’s question about how phones locate which lane of a highway a car is on in areas without cell service. Google says the new model also has improved language understanding “across all supported AI Mode languages.”

Users have more thinking level options with Gemini 4 Hydrogen, as well, including low, medium, high, and a new “xhigh” mode. According to Google, the new model “delivers significant leaps in both speed and intelligence” compared to Gemini Flash 3.8, and it “matches or outperforms some of the competing models in its class,” like Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Terra.

highlights.title: Microsoft Struggling to Fix Global System Outage Impacting Email Systems and More, Admits Initial Repairs 'Not Taking as Expected'
highlights.summary: Microsoft is struggling to fix a prolonged systems outage that has hindered access to online services including Outlook and Teams. On the upside, AI tool Copilot has also been impacted.
body: For more than 12 hours, users around the world have been reporting an inability to access email accounts, instant messaging systems, and documents via OneDrive and Office365. No Xbox services are believed to be offline, however.

Microsoft was quick to acknowledge the problem and admit that it was suffering from issues with its server capabilities, with "elevated load across multiple regions." Attempts to solve this were initially unsuccessful, however, as the company reported its fixes were "not taking as expected."

"We've monitored the status of the changes applied to improve serviceability and confirmed they're not taking as expected," Microsoft said in a lengthy thread on X/Twitter. "We're identifying alternate workstreams that can be applied to increase capacity in the face of sustained traffic management imbalances."
Hours later, Microsoft seemed to have changed tack and was now trying to carve out the impacted servers completely as it struggled to make progress.

highlights.title: Experience: I was disembowelled by a hippo on my honeymoon
highlights.summary: A mother hippopotamus protecting her young is one of the most fearsome forces of nature. Luckily, I’d just married someone ready to meet it head-on. Anna and I got married in Portugal in September last year. We had been together for 13 years.
body: Ten days later, I found myself in a swamp in Botswana with my intestines hanging out of my back.
We were on our honeymoon in the Okavango Delta. That evening, we had set off with a group in traditional canoes. We weren’t looking for hippos; the excursion was supposed to be about plants.

Before we left, we were warned that a mother hippo with two babies was nearby, so we would stay away from her. I spotted the hippo in the distance and zoomed in to take a photo – she was huge, her open mouth showing big teeth; the calves were behind her.

Our canoe had drifted away from the others. Suddenly, I heard a noise behind us – splashing, grunting, growling. The boat started rocking. I turned to my left and saw the same hippo, mouth still open, charging. The look on the guide’s face was one I will never forget: sheer terror.

highlights.title: Inside the 42-Year Journey to Bring ‘Neuromancer’ to the Screen
highlights.summary: William Gibson released his seminal novel Neuromancer in 1984. WIRED has an exclusive look at how it eventually made its way to Apple TV—thanks in no small part to Drake.
body: Briana Middleton has something to show me. “Wait!” she says just as we’re about to end our Zoom call, reaching for something just beyond her screen.

“When I found out we were going to be doing this,” she says, “I was at the thrift shop in my neighborhood and I found this.” Then she points it at the camera: an issue of WIRED from 1995 featuring Keanu Reeves on the cover alongside the line “ William Gibson on the making of Johnny Mnemonic.”

Very apropos. The 1995 film Johnny Mnemonic was based on a short story by Gibson, who also wrote the screenplay. Molly, the “razorgirl” Middleton plays in Apple TV’s forthcoming Neuromancer adaptation, made her first appearance in that short story. Her relationship with the protagonist Case, played in the series by Callum Turner, mirrors the one Reeves’ Neo had with Trinity in The Matrix, which is steeped in Gibsoneque lore.

body: Three technologies developed by MIT Lincoln Laboratory are among recipients of 2026 R&D 100 Awards. The awards recognize the 100 most significant innovations that have transitioned to use or been made available for license in the past year.

R&D World, an online publication, manages the awards program, which has run annually since 1963. The worldwide competition is judged by an independent panel of science and technology experts and industry professionals.

The laboratory's winners overcome obstacles to improving the security and capability of systems. One technology is an operating system designed to protect embedded computers from cyberattacks. Another technology is a platform for integrating superconductor and semiconductor chips in a wafer-scale system for quantum or high-performance computing. The final winner is an algorithm that removes interference 5G base stations incur on co-channel radio frequency (RF) devices.

highlights.summary: England meekly offer Australia respite from the ongoing sandpaper scandal by being bowled out for 131 in the first one-day international in Perth.
body: Hours after Pat Cummins emphatically hit back at Usman Khawaja's comments, Harry Brook's England folded as 21-year-old fast bowler Mahli Beardman emerged with a stunning 6-24 on his ODI debut.
Beardman nicked off Brook in his second over for his first international wicket. Less than two hours later, bowling accurately and at good pace, he had the best figures by an Australian on ODI debut.
His second ODI wicket was the prized scalp of Joe Root for 17 and he also dismissed Jordan Cox and Sam Curran in an opening spell of five overs that returned figures of 5-18.

Ben Duckett, Tom Banton and Root, plus Beardman's later victims Liam Dawson and Jofra Archer, fell driving in Perth – dismissals familiar from England's wretched start to last winter's Ashes series on the same ground.

body: Some consumers hold out for a special edition console, which might come with a game and special visual enhancements. Over the years, Nintendo has done a great job of delivering in this area, going back to the colorful “Play It Loud” versions of the original Game Boy and some tempting Nintendo 64 variants. More recently, Nintendo has offered several beautiful designs for the Switch, and just kicked things off on the Switch 2. Here are six of the best-looking special editions.

You might expect a lot of color from a special edition modeled after a game like Splatoon 3, and mostly that’s what you get (along with the OLED version of the hardware, for added brightness). The system’s base itself is white with gray print, featuring an intricate design that is enhanced by a splotch of bright yellow “paint” on its left portion. The base looks like it just got pegged by a paintball. The JoyCons, meanwhile, are vibrant tones of purple and blue on the left side, and green and yellow on the right, also with neat artwork. The effect is very pretty, even if you aren’t super familiar with the IP.
